results.fact: Season window (June)
results.correct_value: June ascents happen with snow on the route; the season column (Jun-Sep with a snow caveat) and a 'risky' June are consistent. The avalanche note's claim that the route is climbed only in a dry Jul-Sep window is the one wrong statement.
results.evidence: A 2018 ascent summited on June 12 with continuous snow from about 6,400 ft and snow runnels on the traverse; a 2014 party summited on May 31 with the summit gully snow-filled. So June is within the climbed season, as the season column says, but snowy, as the June 'risky' rating says; only the avalanche zone text ('climbed only in dry Jul-Sep window') is contradicted.

results.fact: Whether the standard line has a Class 4 step
results.correct_value: The standard line (south ridge, west-face traverse, final southwest gully) is loose Class 3 with short Class 3+ steps; Class 4 is only on the optional west rib or on the southwest face if a party traverses too far.
results.evidence: One trip report says the party drifted onto the southwest face, which 'becomes Class 4 in a hurry', retreated to the last gully to the south and found it 'loose but never more than Class 3'. A second report describes sustained 4th class only on the west rib (an optional harder line) and class 3 rock in the final gully. The beta, approach, waypoint directions and approach variant already say this; rope_note, obj_haz and the itinerary put a Class 4 step on the standard line.

results.fact: Season window
results.evidence: Ascents are documented in mid-June (2015, with steep snow requiring a rope) and early August (2017, glacier largely melted to a snowfield); one source says the Lewis Glacier line is good in early season. No two sources state a best window or whether October belongs in the season, so neither the itinerary's June-August nor the Jul-Oct season column vs the 'Jul-Sep' October note can be settled. Would settle: two published route descriptions giving the season window.

results.fact: Main camp for this route
results.evidence: Both camps genuinely serve Corteo: one party camped on the larch bench above Lewis Lake for Corteo alone, another camped at Wing Lake and climbed both Black and Corteo from there. Wing Lake serves this route mainly when combined with Black Peak; Lewis Lake bench is the itinerary's camp and the natural one for Corteo alone. Bivy list is owned by the camping clean-up; no patch.
